{{Short description|Concept in functional analysis}}
In [[functional analysis]], a '''topological homomorphism''' or simply '''homomorphism''' (if no confusion will arise) is the analog of [[homomorphism]]s for the category of [[topological vector space]]s (TVSs). 
This concept is of considerable importance in functional analysis and the famous [[Open mapping theorem (functional analysis)|open mapping theorem]] gives a sufficient condition for a continuous linear map between [[Fréchet space]]s to be a topological homomorphism. 

== Definitions ==

A '''topological homomorphism''' or simply '''homomorphism''' (if no confusion will arise) is a [[Continuous map|continuous]] [[linear map]] <math>u : X \to Y</math> between [[topological vector space]]s (TVSs) such that the induced map <math>u : X \to \operatorname{Im} u</math> is an [[open mapping]] when <math>\operatorname{Im} u := u(X),</math> which is the [[Image (mathematics)|image]] of <math>u,</math> is given the [[subspace topology]] induced by <math>Y.</math>{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=74–78}} 
This concept is of considerable importance in functional analysis and the famous [[Open mapping theorem (functional analysis)|open mapping theorem]] gives a sufficient condition for a continuous linear map between [[Fréchet space]]s to be a topological homomorphism. 

A '''TVS embedding'''{{anchor|TVS-embedding|TVS embedding|topological vector space embedding}} or a '''topological [[monomorphism]]'''{{sfn|Köthe|1969|p=91}} is an [[Injective map|injective]] topological homomorphism. Equivalently, a TVS-embedding is a linear map that is also a [[topological embedding]].

== Characterizations ==

Suppose that <math>u : X \to Y</math> is a linear map between TVSs and note that <math>u</math> can be decomposed into the composition of the following canonical linear maps: 

:<math>X ~\overset{\pi}{\rightarrow}~ X / \operatorname{ker} u ~\overset{u_0}{\rightarrow}~ \operatorname{Im} u ~\overset{\operatorname{In}}{\rightarrow}~ Y</math>

where <math>\pi : X \to X / \operatorname{ker} u</math> is the canonical [[quotient map]] and <math>\operatorname{In} : \operatorname{Im} u \to Y</math> is the [[inclusion map]]. 

The following are equivalent:
#<math>u</math> is a topological homomorphism
#for every neighborhood base <math>\mathcal{U}</math> of the origin in <math>X,</math> <math>u\left( \mathcal{U} \right)</math> is a neighborhood base of the origin in <math>Y</math>{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=74–78}}
#the induced map <math>u_0 : X / \operatorname{ker} u \to \operatorname{Im} u</math> is an isomorphism of TVSs{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=74–78}}

If in addition the range of <math>u</math> is a finite-dimensional Hausdorff space then the following are equivalent:
#<math>u</math> is a topological homomorphism
#<math>u</math> is continuous{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=74–78}}
#<math>u</math> is continuous at the origin{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=74–78}}
#<math>u^{-1}(0)</math> is closed in <math>X</math>{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=74–78}}

== Sufficient conditions ==

{{Math theorem|name=Theorem{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=74–78}}|math_statement=
Let <math>u : X \to Y</math> be a surjective continuous linear map from an [[LF-space]] <math>X</math> into a TVS <math>Y.</math> 
If <math>Y</math> is also an [[LF-space]] or if <math>Y</math> is a [[Fréchet space]] then <math>u : X \to Y</math> is a topological homomorphism.
}}

{{Math theorem|name=Theorem{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|p=116}}|math_statement=
Suppose <math>f : X \to Y</math> be a continuous linear operator between two Hausdorff TVSs. If <math>M</math> is a dense vector subspace of <math>X</math> and if the restriction <math>f\big\vert_M : M \to Y</math> to <math>M</math> is a topological homomorphism then <math>f : X \to Y</math> is also a topological homomorphism.{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|p=116}} 

So if <math>C</math> and <math>D</math> are Hausdorff completions of <math>X</math> and <math>Y,</math> respectively, and if <math>f : X \to Y</math> is a topological homomorphism, then <math>f</math>'s unique continuous linear extension <math>F : C \to D</math> is a topological homomorphism. (However, it is possible for <math>f : X \to Y</math> to be surjective but for <math>F : C \to D</math> to <em>not</em> be injective.)
}}

=== Open mapping theorem ===

The [[Open mapping theorem (functional analysis)|open mapping theorem]], also known as [[Stefan Banach|Banach]]'s homomorphism theorem, gives a sufficient condition for a continuous linear operator between complete metrizable TVSs to be a topological homomorphism. 

{{Math theorem|name=Theorem{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|p=78}}|math_statement=
Let <math>u : X \to Y</math> be a continuous linear map between two complete metrizable TVSs. 
If <math>\operatorname{Im} u,</math> which is the range of <math>u,</math> is a dense subset of <math>Y</math> then either <math>\operatorname{Im} u</math> is [[Meager set|meager]] (that is, [[Meagre set|of the first category]]) in <math>Y</math> or else <math>u : X \to Y</math> is a surjective topological homomorphism. 
In particular, <math>u : X \to Y</math> is a topological homomorphism if and only if <math>\operatorname{Im} u</math> is a closed subset of <math>Y.</math>
}}

{{Math theorem|name=Corollary{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|p=78}}|math_statement=
Let <math>\sigma</math> and <math>\tau</math> be TVS topologies on a vector space <math>X</math> such that each topology makes <math>X</math> into a [[F-space|complete metrizable TVSs]]. If either <math>\sigma \subseteq \tau</math> or <math>\tau \subseteq \sigma</math> then <math>\sigma = \tau.</math>
}}

{{Math theorem|name=Corollary{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|p=78}}|math_statement=
If <math>X</math> is a [[Complete topological vector space|complete]] [[Metrizable topological vector space|metrizable TVS]], <math>M</math> and <math>N</math> are two closed vector subspaces of <math>X,</math> and if <math>X</math> is the algebraic direct sum of <math>M</math> and <math>N</math> (i.e. the direct sum in the category of vector spaces), then <math>X</math> is the direct sum of <math>M</math> and <math>N</math> in the category of topological vector spaces.
}}

== Examples ==

Every [[continuous linear functional]] on a TVS is a topological homomorphism.{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=74–78}}

Let <math>X</math> be a <math>1</math>-dimensional TVS over the field <math>\mathbb{K}</math> and let <math>x \in X</math> be non-zero. Let <math>L : \mathbb{K} \to X</math> be defined by <math>L(s) := s x.</math> If <math>\mathbb{K}</math> has it usual [[Euclidean topology]] and if <math>X</math> is [[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff]] then <math>L : \mathbb{K} \to X</math> is a TVS-isomorphism.
